_note: DEFAULT CATALOG since 2026-09-30 (condor/run_cat_scenarios.sh, condor/submit_cat_range.sh, test/run_small_sample_pipeline.sh); scenario_8_full_pipeline_acc_t030 is the deployed configuration and equals json/example_config.json. json/seven_scenarios_v63_acceptance.json plus the DEPLOYABLE working point of the CT-threshold scan (pipeline-dev/combo_study/threshold_scan/threshold_scan.md): scenario_8_full_pipeline_acc_t030. The scan found a plateau at t = 0.25-0.35 (theta68 7.23-7.24 on the 722 evaluation cats, both eras agreeing) against 7.99 at t = 0.50, so t = 0.30 is the recommendation and t = 0.50 is kept as the validation of the code path against the offline 7.99. scenario_7_full_pipeline_acc_t050 is scenario_7_full_pipeline_acc of the seven-scenario catalog with an explicit name; that catalog is kept as-is because a running campaign uses it. THE TWO ARMS DIFFER ONLY IN (a) the hard CT cut, (b) the burst-axis ES table of that selection and (c) its CC-sourced acceptance R -- all three are properties of the SAME selection and must always move together. The P(ES|CT score) calibration and pi_fixed are measured over the whole score range and are threshold independent, so they are reused unchanged. Scenario 3 is the unchanged regression reference. REBUILD RULE: the acceptance coefficients, the ES table and the purity calibration are properties of the ED model, the CT model and the selection, not of the physics -- rebuild them together and re-run the rotated-R null whenever any of them changes.
